callouts.title: Purpose
callouts.body: Rapid-access reference cards for use during [[Forethought-Phase|Forethought]] and [[Self-Reflection-Phase|Self-Reflection]] sessions. These cards operationalize the language design principles from [[Achievement-Goal-Theory]], [[Self-Determination-Theory]], [[Attribution-Theory]], and [[Formative-Assessment]] research. **Bookmark this note for quick access during sessions.**

callouts.title: Mastery-Framed Goal Formulations
callouts.body: Use right-column language in Forethought Protocol goal-setting. The distinction in each pair is between **stable, global, ability-referenced** language (avoid) and **specific, process-referenced, controllable** language (use). See [[Achievement-Goal-Theory]] and [[Mastery-Goal-Orientation]].

callouts.title: Fill-in-the-blank formulas for specific, evaluable comprehension criteria. See [[The-Fluency-Illusion|why these must require cognitive production, not recognition]].
Use this card whenever you notice a global attribution during Self-Reflection.
callouts.body: Global attributions ("I'm not good at this," "this material is too hard") are the most consequential failure mode in the SRL cycle. They route to [[Defensive-Inference|defensive inferences]] that degrade the next [[Forethought-Phase]]. See [[Attribution-Theory]], [[Bernard-Weiner]], and [[Attribution-Retraining]].

callouts.title: 1. Schema Gap
callouts.body:
"Was there [[Prior-Knowledge|prior knowledge]] that this text assumed I had, that I didn't have?"
- **If yes:** What specific prerequisite reading would address this?
- **Action:** Add to [[SRL-Living-Learning-Agenda]] reading queue

callouts.title: 2. Goal Calibration
callouts.body:
"Was my comprehension criterion appropriately matched to my current schema level?"
- **If too ambitious:** What more proximal criterion would have been achievable?
- **Action:** Adjust goal scope in next Forethought

callouts.title: 3. Strategy Mismatch
callouts.body:
"Did I use the most effective reading strategy for this text type and my schema level?"
- **If no:** Which would have been better?
  - [[Advance-Organizers|Advance organizer activation]]
  - [[Elaborative-Interrogation|Elaborative interrogation]]
  - Self-explanation at section breaks
  - Structural reading before detail
- **Action:** Select and implement alternative strategy

callouts.title: 4. Attention Management
callouts.body:
"Was my attention available for the cognitive demands this text required?"
- **If no:** What environmental or scheduling adjustment would address this?
- **Action:** Modify session conditions

callouts.title: 5. Time/Scope Pressure
callouts.body:
"Did I attempt too much in this session relative to the text's density?"
- **If yes:** What is a more realistic scope for one session?
- **Action:** Reduce scope in next session's Forethought

callouts.title: For any session where process goals were substantially unmet, complete this sentence:
callouts.body:
*"The strategy I used was [specific strategy]. It was insufficient because [specific mechanism]. A better approach for next time would be [specific alternative]."*

This sentence structure makes it structurally difficult to make external or fixed-internal attributions. See [[Mastery-Oriented-Response-Pattern]].

callouts.title: The language you use in self-talk during sessions shapes your [[Achievement-Goal-Theory|goal orientation]]. Performance grammar activates ego-threat; mastery grammar activates learning orientation. See [[Formative-Assessment]] and [[Self-Determination-Theory]].
Even self-directed controlling language undermines [[Intrinsic-Motivation]]. See [[Self-Determination-Theory]] and [[Autonomy-Support]].
Use this checklist to validate that the adaptive inferences you generate in Self-Reflection are genuinely actionable. See [[Adaptive-Inference]].
The Early Implementation Dip Is Normal
callouts.body: Research on [[Deliberate-Practice]] and metacognitive training consistently shows an initial performance dip when implementing explicit self-regulatory strategies. This is expected and temporary — the cognitive overhead of the new protocols competes with resources available for content processing. See [[Cognitive-Load-Theory]].

ordered.text: **Sessions will feel longer** — The protocol adds 15-25 minutes to each session
**Comprehension may temporarily decrease** — This is normal, not evidence of failure
**The protocols will feel awkward** — Like any new skill, fluency develops through practice
**You will want to skip zones** — This is the precise moment to persist

unordered.text: [ ] **Specific** — Names a particular strategy or behavior (not "try harder")
[ ] **Actionable** — Can be entered directly into the next Forethought template
[ ] **Testable** — You can tell whether it worked after the next session
[ ] **Within control** — Depends on your actions, not circumstances
[ ] **Strategy-based** — Addresses HOW you approach the material, not whether you're "capable"
Weeks 1-2: Implement Zone 1 (Prior Knowledge) and Zone 3 (Goal Setting) from Forethought only
Weeks 3-4: Add Zone 1 (Cold Reconstruction) from Self-Reflection
**Do NOT implement the full protocol immediately**
Count a session as successful if you **executed the protocol with integrity** — regardless of comprehension outcome
This maintains [[Self-Efficacy]] during the adaptation period
Note when zones become easier to complete
The visible record of practice IS the [[Self-Efficacy|mastery experience]]
